'''Crypto1''' is a proprietary [[encryption]] algorithm ([[stream cipher]]) and authentication protocol created by [[NXP Semiconductors]] for its [[Mifare|MIFARE]] Classic [[RFID]] [[Contactless smart card|contactless smart cards]] launched in 1994. Such cards have been used in many notable systems, including [[Oyster card]], [[CharlieCard]] and [[OV-chipkaart]].

By 2009, cryptographic research had [[Reverse engineering|reverse engineered]] the cipher and a variety of attacks were published that effectively broke the security.<ref>{{cite web |last = de Koning Gans |first = Gerhard |author2 = J.-H. Hoepman |author3      = F.D. NXP responded by issuing "hardened" (but still backwards compatible) cards, the MIFARE Classic EV1. However, in 2015 a new attack rendered the cards insecure,<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Meijer|first1=Carlo|last2=Verdult|first2=Roel|title=Proceedings of the 22nd ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security |chapter=Ciphertext-only Cryptanalysis on Hardened Mifare Classic Cards |date=2015-10-12|chapter-url=https://doi.org/10.1145/2810103.2813641|series=CCS '15|location=Denver, Colorado, USA|publisher=Association for Computing Machinery|pages=18–30|doi=10.1145/2810103.2813641|isbn=978-1-4503-3832-5|hdl=2066/151451|s2cid=4412174|hdl-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last1=Meijer|last2=Verdult|title=Ciphertext-only Cryptanalysis on Hardened Mifare Classic|url=http://www.cs.ru.nl/R.Verdult/Ciphertext-only_Cryptanalysis_on_Hardened_Mifare_Classic_Cards-CCS_2015.pdf|url-status=live|website=R. Verdult's page at Institute for Computing and Information Sciences, [[Radboud University]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210429181134/http://www.cs.ru.nl/R.Verdult/Ciphertext-only_Cryptanalysis_on_Hardened_Mifare_Classic_Cards-CCS_2015.pdf |archive-date= 2021-04-29}}</ref> and NXP recommended migrating away from Mifare Classic.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Grüll|first=Johannes|date=October 12, 2015|title=Security Statement on Crypto1 Implementations |url= https://www.mifare.net/en/products/chip-card-ics/mifare-classic/security-statement-on-crypto1-implementations/ |access-date=2021-04-29|website= Mifare | publisher = NXD}}</ref>

{{See also|MIFARE#Security}}

== Technical description ==
Crypto1 is a [[stream cipher]] very similar in its structure to its successor, Hitag2. Crypto1 consists of
* a 48-bit [[LFSR|linear feedback shift register]] for the state of the cipher,
* a two-layer 20-to-1 nonlinear function used to generate the keystream, and
* a 16-bit LFSR which is used during the authentication phase as a [[pseudo random number generator]]

The usual operation of Crypto1 and Hitag2 ciphers uses nonlinear feedback only during the initialization/authentication stage, switching to operation as a LFSR with a nonlinear output filter (filter generator) for the rest of the communications.
